note: Independent check of the outside MicroLens++ probe (coordinator's review, 2026-11-13): three lens reports (construction, numbers, implications) and a final skeptic; model output, kept for traceability.

claims.reasoning: FILES SHOW: the three numbers are in the JSON (T3_perp.J_lens: share 0.3449; random mean 0.0899, p95 0.2040). Code: share and baseline at mlpp_probe.py:163-172 (200 Gaussian directions made Euclidean-perp to the foreign span, seed 7; only mean and p95 are stored, line 172). There is no uncertainty on 0.345: per-prompt differences are averaged away at line 138, the axes cache of line 126 is not in the repo, and there is no bootstrap or split-half. INFERENCE: against the isotropic null the value is extreme (a Beta(2, 20.3) reproduces the stored mean and p95; tail probability of 0.345 about 1.5e-3), so it is not isotropic chance. That null is the wrong comparison for the residual of a text-derived mean difference: a Gaussian direction has 0.2 % of its Euclidean energy in the foreign span before projection, raw u_T has 36.9 % (JSON euclid.foreign_share_u_T_raw), and the null directions share no prompts, pipeline or data covariance with the axes. Three observations from the JSON itself: (a) by the same baseline the logit-lens share (0.032) is MORE extreme than the J-lens one (6.2x the mean and 2.5x the p95, against 3.8x and 1.7x), so an excess appears under any non-Euclidean metric; (b) raw u_T has a LOWER M_J share (0.290) than u_T_perp (0.345), although in T4 raw u_T moves the foreign word sets 1.3 to 7 times more, so the share is not a validated measure of foreign use; (c) the share equals ||F(c - c_M)||^2_M / ||u_E||^2_M, the disagreement between the Euclidean and the M_J regression coefficients (identity checked numerically). A synthetic world in which u_T_perp has exactly zero content on every foreign topic direction reproduces a share of 0.33-0.35 against an isotropic baseline of 0.08 / 0.24 (see issues).

FILES SHOW: cosines -0.4901 / -0.5517 / -0.4650 with sports / tone / sea and +0.3730 with NEG (the README prints -0,47 for sea; correct rounding is -0,46). ALGEBRA (checked numerically): with c the Euclidean and c_M the M-metric regression coefficients of u on the foreign axes F, F^T M u_E = (F^T M F)(c_M - c). Because u_E is Euclidean-orthogonal to f, <u_E, f>_M = sum_k (lambda_k - L) u_Ek f_k for ANY constant L: the M inner product only says how the zero-sum coordinate products are spread over high- and low-gain eigen-directions. For one axis, c_M - c = Cov(lambda_k, u_k / f_k) / E[lambda_k] with weights f_k^2. So 'negative' means: u resembles the foreign axes more in low-gain than in high-gain directions, and the Euclidean projection removes more of the common foreign mode than the M_J projection would. That is true relative to M_J by construction and is consistent with the JSON (Euclidean share of raw u_T 0.369 against M_J share 0.290). It is not a statement about sports, sea or tone content. The four cosines are close to one degree of freedom: sum of cos^2 is 0.90 but the share is 0.345, and Cauchy-Schwarz on these five numbers gives a mean sign-aligned M_J cosine of at least 0.52 among the four foreign axes (NEG with flipped sign). T4 does not confirm M_J as the yardstick: tone has the most negative cosine (-0.55) but the smallest behavioural overshoot (odd part -0.18, against sports -0.27 and sea -0.23), and the M_J-orthogonal axis leaves tone at +0.71. T3 is also symmetric: in the Euclidean and logit-lens metrics the J perp is the one with foreign overlap (cos +0.30 / +0.33 / +0.30 and +0.25 / +0.27 / +0.23). What T4 does give: the odd parts of u_T_perp are negative for all three sets, so 'overshoots zero' has sign support in one run without error bars.

FILES SHOW: numbers match JSON T4_use (the README's +0,39 for sports is 0.3846, a double rounding). The effect is the mean over positions of the change of log P(word set) on the 64 teacher-forced unsteered reference continuations (mlpp_probe.py:193-201); sets of 8-10 words (lines 178-182; a tokenizer-only check confirms all 34 are single tokens). ODD / EVEN SPLIT (computed from the JSON): u_T_perp odd: RSI +0.631, sports -0.271, sea -0.234, tone -0.178 (43 %, 37 %, 28 % of the RSI part, opposite sign). Even: +0.106, +0.113, +0.097, +0.123: a push of EITHER sign raises all four sets, RSI included, by about 0.11 nats. The sign pattern survives; 29 %, 29 % and 41 % of the quoted +0.39 / +0.33 / +0.30 are non-directional, the directional sizes are 0.27 / 0.23 / 0.18, and the plus/minus asymmetry of the README is entirely the even part. LIMITS OF THE INFERENCE: (1) no interval and no null: one run, per-sequence values discarded (line 201), no random-direction control (line 210 pushes four vectors only), no neutral word set, no push along the foreign axes themselves. The damage calibration alone implies a probability-weighted SD of per-token log-probability shifts of sqrt(2 x 0.05) = 0.32 nats; a toy null (iid logit shifts at 0.05 nats, 8 random rare tokens) gives an odd-part SD of 0.17 and a 95 % range of 0.33. Foreign odd parts of 0.18-0.27 lie inside it. (2) All three foreign sets move by a similar amount, as a common term would make them (the log-softmax normaliser is shared by every rare token); the README's rebuttal via the J perp rules out a redistribution of RSI-word mass, not this direction-dependent term. (3) 'Pushes the model toward the control topics' is a claim about text; the measure is a factor exp(0.27) = 1.31 on the geometric-mean probability of a small set on unsteered text. At a base probability of 1e-4 per position that is 0.08 extra words over all 64 texts (0.8 at 1e-3); base probabilities are not stored and nothing was generated. (4) Several set members are generic or on-topic for the prompts (' game', ' team', ' match', ' water', ' great', ' love'; prompts on the sea, a river, rain, chess engines, a team: rk_loop.py:59-84).

FILES SHOW: numbers match (the README's +0,05 for sports under the minus push is 0.0449). Odd parts of the J-metric perp: RSI +0.655, sports +0.033, sea +0.058, tone +0.710; even +0.06 to +0.08. So in odd terms the axis is near zero for sports and sea (5 % and 9 % of the RSI part) and moves tone words more than RSI words (108 %). The descriptive half of the claim holds for this run. INFERENCE: 'neutral' is a point estimate without interval or null, on one hand-picked word list per topic (same limits as C3). For tone there is a definition mismatch: the tone set contains '!' (token id 0, mlpp_probe.py:181), and the vocabulary filter of line 53 removes '!' from the rows that define M_J (tokenizer check: it is the only one of the 34 set tokens outside the filtered vocabulary). If '!' carries most of the set's probability (not stored, so unverified), the J perp was never made orthogonal to it, and 'not neutral for tone' is not evidence that RSI and tone are entangled in the model's reading. Whatever the cause, the result contradicts the premise of T3: M_J-orthogonality to an axis (cosine 5e-17 by construction) does not give a neutral use test, and the M_J perp's tone effect is the largest foreign effect in the table apart from raw u_T.

FILES SHOW: the score exists only in the probe (mlpp_probe.py:212) and is signed: e_rsi - max(e_foreign) for the plus push, -e_rsi - max(-e_foreign) for the minus push. Recomputed: 0.79 / 0.83 for u_T_perp, -0.06 / -0.05 for the J perp. By arithmetic a signed score pays a bonus for foreign effects opposite to the RSI effect (+0.055 and +0.301 here); that half of the claim is true of this score. INFERENCE: (1) neither round uses such a score. Round 1: D4 = |c_4| - max |cos_x| (rk_verdict.py:74, required > 0 at line 87) and |z| < 2.58 for sports and literature behaviour (lines 81-83). Round 2: m_X = |change| / gap < 0.5 m_concept (plan line 1624; r2_unlearn_qwen.py:137 and 222-223). All are two-sided, so an anti-component counts against. (2) The contrast the README draws does not come from the bonus: the J perp scores -0.06 because tone moves as much as RSI. With a two-sided score (RSI minus max |foreign|) the Euclidean perp still wins: +0.58 / +0.14 on the raw numbers, +0.36 against -0.06 on odd parts. (3) 'Foreign effect about 0' is a sound demand, but under it the Euclidean perp is closer to 0 than the J perp on the maximum (0.27 against 0.71), the RMS (0.23 against 0.41) and the sum (0.68 against 0.80) of the foreign odd parts. The part that is new relative to the plan: both rounds use relative thresholds, not an equivalence interval around 0.

FILES SHOW: overlap_logit_vs_J_top15 = 1 ('myself'), computed as a set intersection of stripped strings (mlpp_probe.py:61 and 157). INFERENCE: partly an artefact of the definition. The J-lens list has 'learning' twice (two token ids) and seven forms of analy-; the logit-lens list has five forms of learn-. Distinct 5-letter stems: 10 and 7, shared stems 2 (learn, myself); 6 of 15 logit-lens entries and 3 of 15 J-lens entries have a stem in the other list. In the filtered vocabulary 32 % of tokens share their stripped string with another token (55 % ignoring case; tokenizer check), so top lists fill with variants. The statistic is unstable inside one lens too: the J-lens top-15 of u_T_perp and of the J perp (Euclidean cosine 0.91) share 3 strings, and the logit-lens list of u_T_perp shares 4 with the J-lens list of the J perp, more than with the J-lens list of u_T_perp itself. So 1 of 15 is close to the same-lens variation between similar vectors. Both lenses read the SAME position (logit lens: direct unembedding; J-lens: through the remaining blocks at that position, as extract.py:21 and 29-30 use it); neither measures what later tokens read, so the last sentence of the README's point 4 does not follow. That the logit lens and the J-lens differ at block 14 of 28 is the known reason the J-lens exists. A cosine or rank correlation of the two full readout vectors would be the right statistic.

FILES SHOW: cos(all tokens, semantic tokens) = 0.9957 / 0.9872 / 0.9796 / 0.9912 / 0.9663 for rsi / sports / tone / sea / neg and 0.9910 for u_T_perp; non-semantic token share 12.3-16.2 %; T4 odd parts of the filtered axis differ from the unfiltered one by at most 0.03 (RSI 0.650 against 0.631, sports -0.277 against -0.271, sea -0.206 against -0.234, tone -0.174 against -0.178). The claim holds for the POSITION filter, which is what the README states. NOT TESTED: T3 for the filtered axis, and the effect of the VOCABULARY filter and centring on M_J. That filter keeps 93,898 of 151,936 rows, drops all 25,557 CJK tokens and all punctuation-only tokens, and keeps 13,133 tokens that begin with punctuation (the JSON's raw-axis list contains '!I'); it does interact with one result (the tone set, see C4).

TRUE PART: u_T_perp, the fixed axes of O1 and WriteOrth are Euclidean constructions, and neither round uses a lens metric. FALSE PART: 'zero by construction, visible in no indicator' (README lines 14-15). Round 1's cos_sports / cos_tone / cos_sea are cosines of the RESPONSE direction d_(n+1), the mean read-state difference of the texts generated under the plus and the minus push (rk_loop.py:285, 314, 317), with the raw foreign axes. Only the pushed d_0 is orthogonal by construction. If a minus push made texts more sporty, cos(d_1, sports) would be negative, and D4 = |c| - max |cos_x| (rk_verdict.py:74) counts it against. Round 1 also has a behavioural foreign check that is not Euclidean geometry at all: K5 uses gradients of Yes/No log-odds for sports and literature statements as reading covectors, with |z| < 2.58 required (rk_loop.py:346-366, 453; rk_verdict.py:81-83). Round 2's OD-C6 is the absolute change of the mean projection of the GENERATED, re-read instructed texts on each foreign axis in units of that axis's own gap (plan line 1624; r2_unlearn_qwen.py:133-139, rule at 222-223), with a signed descriptive version at line 882. These are measurements on output texts in the frame in which the foreign axes were calibrated; they are two-sided and not blind. WHAT IS RIGHT IN EFFECT: the thresholds are relative (D4 > 0; m_X < 0.5 m_concept), so a foreign movement of 28-43 % of the concept movement would be reported but would pass. Whether the probe's log-probability shift reaches text level at all is open (C3). On the probe's own T4 the Euclidean perp has smaller foreign effects than the J perp in aggregate, so replacing or supplementing the Euclidean criterion by M_J is not supported either. I read no round-1 output.

issues.title: Round 1 and round 2 foreign controls are measured on generated texts and are two-sided; they are not zero by construction
issues.detail: The README's 'structural error' rests on the sentence that the foreign cosines are zero by construction and the leak is visible in no indicator. Code: rk_loop.py:317 computes cos(dn, raw foreign axis) for dn = delta[ok].mean(0) (line 285), the read-state response of texts generated under the push (line 314); rk_verdict.py:74 uses absolute values and line 87 requires D4 > 0; K5 (rk_loop.py:346-366, 453; rk_verdict.py:81-83) is a gradient-based behavioural check on sports and literature statements. Round 2: r2_unlearn_qwen.py:133-139 (absolute change of the projection of generated texts, in gap units), rule at 222-223, plan lines 1218-1219, 1240-1241 and 1624. Only the cosine of u_T_perp itself with the foreign axes is zero by construction. The probe's prediction is therefore testable in existing output: it implies clearly negative cos(d_1, sports / sea / tone) for the RSI loops.

issues.title: T4: a third of the quoted counter-steering effect is non-directional, and the J perp is not the more neutral axis
issues.detail: Odd (o) and even (e) parts from the JSON, order RSI / sports / sea / tone. u_T_perp: o +0.631 / -0.271 / -0.234 / -0.178, e +0.106 / +0.113 / +0.097 / +0.123. J perp: o +0.655 / +0.033 / +0.058 / +0.710, e +0.062 / +0.078 / +0.072 / +0.070. Filtered: o +0.650 / -0.277 / -0.206 / -0.174, e about +0.11. Raw u_T: o +0.797 / +0.529 / +0.312 / +1.301, e +0.07 to +0.10. The even part is the same for every set and every construction (0.06-0.12), which is what damage does to rare tokens; the README's minus-push numbers include it. Foreign odd parts as a share of the RSI odd part: u_T_perp -43 / -37 / -28 %; J perp +5 / +9 / +108 %; raw +66 / +39 / +163 %. Max, RMS and sum of the foreign odd parts: 0.27 / 0.23 / 0.68 for u_T_perp against 0.71 / 0.41 / 0.80 for the J perp. Assuming a linear response and using the alphas and norms in the JSON, the foreign effect crosses zero at 89 % (sports), 80 % (sea) and 20 % (tone) of the way from the Euclidean to the J perp: two word sets favour the M_J zero point, the one with the largest effects favours the Euclidean one, and no point on that line is neutral for all three. In the same units 38 % of the raw axis's RSI-word response sits in its foreign-span part, so the word sets are not cleanly separable. Surviving statements: the sign of the anti-effect for u_T_perp, near-zero sports and sea for the J perp, tone not neutral for the J perp, raw u_T unspecific. Not surviving: the sizes +0.39 / +0.33 / +0.30, and 'the more neutral J-perpendicular axis'.

issues.title: T3 cannot tell over-subtracted topics from one shared loud direction (algebra and synthetic counterexamples)
issues.detail: Every T3 number is a function of the Euclidean and the M_J Gram of five vectors; topic-specific readouts do not enter. Synthetic check (numpy only, D = 2048, spectrum lambda_k ~ (k+1)^-1.13 matched to the reported entropy rank 227 and to the baseline scale of about 45): foreign axes = own topic direction + one shared mode made of a quiet part and a small part on a lens-loud direction; u_T_perp = RSI direction + t (loud - kappa quiet), which is Euclidean-orthogonal to the foreign axes and has EXACTLY zero content on every foreign topic direction. A fit of 10 scalars reproduces all twelve T3 numbers to within 0.030-0.045 on four random seeds: M-cosines about -0.48 / -0.53 / -0.48 / +0.40, M share 0.33-0.35, Euclidean share of raw 0.369, M share of raw 0.290, cos_E(u_E, u_J) 0.89, cos_E(u_J, f) about 0.30 / 0.34 / 0.29 / -0.22, isotropic baseline 0.08 / 0.24. The whole signature is carried by a component with 5.7-7.1 % of u_T_perp's Euclidean norm (0.3-0.5 % of its squared norm, 57 % of its M-norm); without it the cosines are 0.00-0.07. In that world the J perp is the axis that contains foreign topic content (0.10-0.23 of the RSI coordinate). Converse world: a raw axis with no foreign topic content that shares only the quiet mode gets real negative topic content from the Euclidean projection (-0.31 to -0.45), while the M-cosines are about 0 (share 0.001-0.06, below the isotropic mean) or +0.3, depending on a loud coordinate of 0.08 against 0.12. If the shared mode is less loud the needed component grows: 16 % of the norm for a mode spread over the top 8 eigen-directions, 25 % for the top 40 (fit error up to 0.08). For isotropic directions the size is not reachable: 2,000 random Euclidean-orthogonal pairs give an M-cosine SD of 0.14 and a maximum of 0.47. This is an existence proof, not a finding about Qwen: the real M_J was not formed (weights not loaded).

issues.title: The isotropic baseline of T3 is not a fair null
issues.detail: Random Gaussian directions control for the anisotropy of M_J and the dimension of the span, not for being a text-derived mean difference from the same prompts and pipeline, nor for being the residual of a direction that had 37 % of its energy in the span. Fair baselines, all without forward passes once per-prompt read states exist: (a) each foreign axis made Euclidean-perp to the other three and to u_T, with its M_J share and cosines; (b) the 2,000 within-prompt sign-flip null axes that round 1 already builds and projects (rk_loop.py:223, 226, 230); (c) prompt bootstrap and split-half of the four cosines and the share; (d) placebo topic axes from new instruction pairs. In the synthetic world, (a) gives shares of 0.03-0.42 with cosines up to 0.6 for the foreign axes among themselves, so the RSI value is unremarkable there; null directions with 3x or 10x the isotropic variance along the shared loud mode reach a share of 0.345 in 9.5 % or 32 % of draws, against 1 % for isotropic ones. The probe stores neither the 200 baseline draws nor the foreign-foreign Gram, the raw axis's M_J cosines or any M-norm ratio, and the axes cache is not in the repo, so none of this can be recomputed from the committed files.

issues.title: What an M_J cosine is, and what dominates it
issues.detail: cos_MJ(a, b) is the cosine between two predicted logit-shift patterns over 93,898 filtered tokens with equal weight per token. It differs from 'the metric the model reads with' in four ways: an average same-position Jacobian fitted on 466 wikitext prompts of 128 tokens (config.yaml), not on chat text; the final RMSNorm replaced by its gain only (mlpp_probe.py:54), without the normalisation Jacobian; uniform weight over the vocabulary rather than the probability-weighted Fisher metric that governs KL and log-probability changes; a filter that drops 38 % of the rows, including '!' and all CJK tokens (line 53). Lens file alone (no weights loaded): J[14] has one dominant mode, singular value 102.7 against 20.2 for the next, 44.9 % of the squared Frobenius norm (participation ratio 4.9; 202 without that mode). Its output side sits on about 5 final-layer coordinates (1793, 1999, 1683 with weights 0.53, 0.52, 0.46), exactly where a gain-only linearisation of the final norm is least trustworthy. The reported entropy rank 227 and the baseline scale of 45 are consistent with one mode holding 10-15 % of tr(M_J) plus a broad bulk; this is an inference, since the unembedding was not loaded. In such a metric a component with about 6 % of a vector's Euclidean norm on that mode weighs as much as all the rest. The condition number 1.6e11 carries no information for cosines: J is stored in fp16, whose rounding noise (spectral norm about 2e-3) exceeds the smallest singular value (1.8e-4). The file has no provenance key, so capture point and position handling cannot be read from it.

issues.title: T4 has no interval, no null and no controls
issues.detail: One run; 64 continuations (32 RSI-topic and 32 scene prompts, not reported separately); the axes are themselves one random draw of sampled texts; per-sequence effects are discarded (mlpp_probe.py:201), so no bootstrap is possible afterwards. Missing: random or covariance-matched directions at matched damage (round 1 uses 16 for K6), frequency-matched neutral word sets, more than one word list per topic, a push along each foreign axis as positive control and scale, baseline P(set). What one run supports: paired comparisons between constructions on the same texts are stable (the 0.991-cosine filtered axis reproduces every odd part within 0.03; even parts agree across sets within an SD of 0.011), so the differences between the Euclidean and the J perp on these texts and word lists are real. What it does not support: generalisation to other prompts, word lists, axis draws or seeds, any statement of significance against arbitrary directions, and any statement about text. The plus and minus alphas differ by 6 % for the J perp (0.0943 against 0.1000, damage 0.0521); the effect on the odd / even split is below 0.02.

issues.title: The tone word set contains a token that the J metric cannot see
issues.detail: WORDS['tone'] starts with '!' (mlpp_probe.py:181); the regex of line 53 keeps only tokens with a letter or digit, so '!' (id 0) is not among the rows of M_J. The J perp is orthogonal to the tone axis only on the filtered vocabulary. The log-sum-exp of a set is dominated by its most probable member, and per-token effects are not stored, so the share of '!' in the tone result is unknown. Both the README's point 3 (tone entangled with RSI) and the low specificity score of the J perp in point 2 depend on this one set.

issues.title: Mean log-probability of a small word set is not a text-level measure
issues.detail: The statistic weights every position equally, so it is driven by positions where the set is improbable; expected word counts depend on the arithmetic mean probability, which is driven by a few positions where the set is plausible. Odd shifts of 0.18-0.27 nats are factors of 1.2-1.3. At 1e-4 per position that is about 0.05-0.08 extra words over all 64 forty-token texts, at 1e-5 about 0.005-0.008. Free generation can compound or wash out such shifts; only generated text settles it, which is what both rounds measure.

issues.title: Top-15 overlap is a fragile statistic
issues.detail: Exact stripped strings; a duplicate ('learning' twice) and word families leave 10 and 7 distinct stems; same-lens overlap between two vectors of cosine 0.91 is 3 of 15; logit-lens(u_T_perp) against J-lens(J perp) is 4 of 15. Pairwise exact overlaps of all four stored lists: 1, 3, 4, 3, 3, 6.

issues.title: Three figures in the README are double-rounded
issues.detail: cos_MJ(u_T_perp, sea) = -0.46498 is printed as -0,47 (correct -0,46); sports under the minus push 0.38465 as +0,39 (correct +0,38); sports under the minus J-perp push 0.04493 as +0,05 (correct +0,04). They come from rounding the three-decimal log line again. All other 31 checked figures match, including the specificity values, the alpha steps (0.1 x sqrt(0.05 / damage)) and the quadratic scaling of damage with alpha.

recommendations: Measurement 1, T3 offline (no forward passes; needs the per-prompt read states Xp / Xa of the axis texts, which round 1 stores at rk_loop.py:206, its 2,000 sign-flip nulls at 223-230, the lens and the unembedding): (a) the foreign-foreign Gram in the Euclidean and the M_J metric and the raw axis's M_J cosines; (b) the fair nulls: M_J share of the sign-flip null axes after the same projection, and each foreign axis made Euclidean-perp to the others; (c) prompt-bootstrap intervals and split-half values for the four cosines and the share; (d) the contribution of the top 1, 5 and 44 eigen-directions of M_J to each cosine, and what those directions read as; (e) the J-lens PREDICTION of T4: (W_U[ids] g) J v for the four word sets, '!' included, softmax-centred, for all four constructions, against the measured shifts. (e) decides whether the J-lens predicts use at all; (b)-(d) decide whether 0.345 is special and whether it is one loud direction.

Measurement 2, T4 with controls (about 30-60 CPU minutes or a few GPU minutes): store per-sequence effects and report odd parts with prompt-bootstrap intervals; add the 16 null directions of round 1 at matched damage as the null distribution per word set; add three frequency-matched neutral word sets and two more lists per topic, with '!' reported separately; push along sports, sea and tone themselves (positive control, scale, and the 3 x 4 response matrix from which a behaviourally neutral combination can be solved); report baseline P(set) and the change of the arithmetic-mean probability; split RSI-topic and scene prompts.

Measurement 3, text level: the claim that counter-steering pushes toward the control topics predicts clearly negative cos(d_1, sports / sea / tone) in the existing round-1 RSI loop rows (rk_loop.py:317) and a signed foreign movement in round 2's descriptive numbers (r2_unlearn_qwen.py:882), with the SEA and SPO loops as scale. Whoever may read round-1 output can check this at no cost. In addition z_beh(u_T_perp, 'sports') and z_beh(u_T_perp, 'literature') can be computed offline from the stored K5 gradients (rk_loop.py:364-366; line 454 computes the start direction on 'rsi' only): an exact first-order, two-sided behavioural foreign check on the start direction.

Until measurements 1-3 exist, do not change the frozen plan on the basis of this probe and do not use M_J cosines or projections as a criterion. The plan's foreign conditions are already two-sided output measurements; the one transferable suggestion is to report the signed foreign movement with an interval next to the relative threshold, which the scripts already produce descriptively.

If the README is kept: correct the three rounded figures, replace 'zero by construction, visible in no indicator' by the statement that only u_T_perp itself is orthogonal by construction, give the odd and even parts instead of the raw minus-push numbers, and state that the tone set contains a token outside the metric's vocabulary.
reports.summary:
The probe's numbers are in the JSON, but most of its conclusions do not follow from them.

**Numbers.** 31 of 34 checked figures match the JSON. Three are double-rounded (-0.465 printed as -0,47; 0.385 as +0,39; 0.045 as +0,05). The JSON is internally consistent. I did not re-run the probe or load model weights.

**T3 (C1, C2).** The values are extreme against the isotropic baseline (about 1.5e-3), but that baseline is not a fair null for a text-derived residual. The algebra shows the M_J cosines measure only how the Euclidean and M_J regression coefficients disagree. A synthetic world with exactly zero foreign topic content in u_T_perp reproduces all twelve T3 numbers to within 0.03-0.045. The converse world has real topic over-subtraction with M_J cosines of zero or positive sign. The four cosines are close to one degree of freedom. The lens itself has one dominant mode (singular value 102.7 against 20.2) that feeds about five final-layer coordinates.

**T4 (C3-C5).** Odd parts for u_T_perp are RSI +0.63 and sports / sea / tone -0.27 / -0.23 / -0.18. A non-directional +0.11 is common to all four sets and makes up 29-41 % of the quoted counter-steering numbers. The J-metric perp is near zero for sports and sea (+0.03 / +0.06) but +0.71 for tone, so on maximum, RMS and sum the Euclidean perp is the more neutral axis. There is no interval, random-direction null, neutral word set or generated text. The tone set contains "!", which the metric's vocabulary filter excludes. The signed specificity score exists only in the probe; both rounds use two-sided measures.

**C6-C8.**
- **C6:** the count of 1 in 15 is right, but it is a fragile exact-string statistic, and both lenses read the same position.
- **C7:** holds for the position filter.
- **C8:** not supported. Both rounds measure foreign axes on generated, re-read texts and two-sidedly; only u_T_perp itself is orthogonal by construction.

claims.reasoning: Shown by the files: the JSON gives 0.3449 for u_T_perp^E in the J-lens metric and [0.0899, 0.2040] for the random baseline; mlpp_probe.py lines 163-172 compute exactly this, and the formula is algebraically right (on synthetic data the share equals c^T G^-1 c, the largest squared M-cosine with the span). I could not recompute the number: that needs the unembedding and the axes, and no axes cache was delivered. Why only partly: (1) the JSON implies the four foreign axes are almost one direction in this metric. The squared cosines sum to 0.90 but the joint share is 0.345, so the largest eigenvalue of their 4x4 M_J correlation matrix is at least 2.61 of 4. The 'foreign share' is the overlap with one common mode, not with three topics. (2) The lens has a dominant gain direction: 45 % of the squared norm of J[14] sits in one singular direction (sigma 102.7, median 0.98). In a J-only metric that direction alone gives unrelated random directions a share of 0.23 on average (0.58 at the 95th percentile) against four random axes. The probe's own baseline of 0.09 is about 45 times the isotropic value 4/2048; in the logit-lens metric it is 0.005, so the anisotropy comes from J. (3) The baseline is isotropic directions, not text-contrast directions; raw u_T already has 0.290 in this metric. (4) T3 is in-sample, with no cross-fitting or bootstrap; in a synthetic example with true overlap 0, noise in the estimated axis gave measured M-cosines between -0.05 and +0.69. My inference, not shown: the common mode may be the first-person persona voice shared by all instructed contrasts (T1: raw u_T and u_T_perp^J read 'myself, my, ourselves', u_T_perp^E does not).

The cosines are in the JSON (-0.490, -0.552, -0.465; NEG +0.373) and cosM (line 62) is correct. Algebra: u_T_perp^E = u_T_perp^J - F a with a = c_E - c_M, and the M-cosines of u_T_perp^E with the axes have the sign of -(F^T M F) a (checked numerically). So 'subtracts too much' holds by definition relative to the M_J-optimal projection, and it is informative only if M_J is the right yardstick. Because the foreign axes are nearly collinear in M_J (see C1), the three negative cosines are one finding, not three. In favour: in the use test the parts of the effect that follow the sign of the push (half the difference of the + and - rows) are negative for all three word sets for u_T_perp^E: -0.27, -0.23, -0.18 per + push. Against M_J as the yardstick: the axis that is exactly M_J-orthogonal to the tone axis moves tone words by +0.71. No uncertainty estimate, and the measurement is in-sample (see C1, point 4), so neither the sign nor the size is established as more than a property of this one text sample.

The numbers are as stated (JSON T4_use) and the test is built as described: teacher-forced on the 64 unpushed reference texts, push of rk_loop's form, KL matched per direction and sign (lines 184-213). Limits: (1) every word set under every direction carries a rise that does not depend on the sign of the push (half the sum of the + and - rows): +0.06 to +0.12; for u_T_perp^E it is rsi +0.106, sports +0.113, sea +0.097, tone +0.123. It is not a movement toward any topic, and it makes up 29-41 % of the reported +0.39/+0.33/+0.30. My inference is that it comes from taking the log of a summed probability whose tokens respond unequally. The sign-following parts are 0.27, 0.23, 0.18 against 0.63 for RSI words. (2) There are no random word sets and no random directions at matched damage, so 'toward the control topics' is not separated from 'away from the pushed topic, toward everything else'; the three sets move by similar amounts. The README's counter-argument (-u_T_perp^J leaves sports and sea flat) does not settle it, because that axis moves tone words by -0.64. (3) No standard errors over the 64 sequences. (4) The effects are relative changes of mostly small probabilities under teacher forcing. No text was generated under the push, and round 2's C-Q2 pushes instructed texts. ' game', ' team', ' match', ' water' and ' sea' are also ordinary words of several of the 64 prompts (chess engines, a team's way of working, rain, the sound of the sea).

The description matches the JSON: +u_T_perp^J gives sports +0.11, sea +0.13, tone +0.78; -u_T_perp^J gives +0.05, +0.01, -0.64; the sign-following parts are +0.03, +0.06, +0.71. But the test does not cleanly test tone. The tone set contains '!' (token id 0), and line 53 removes every token without a Latin letter or digit from the vocabulary on which M_J is defined, so M_J-orthogonality cannot constrain '!'. How much of the +-0.7 is '!' is not stored. M_J-orthogonality to the tone axis is also not the same as no effect on eight hand-picked tone words, and the 4x4 system that defines u_T_perp^J has nearly collinear columns in M_J. The README's reading (RSI and enthusiastic tone are entangled in the model's reading) is one of several explanations. There are no error bars, so 'neutral' for sports and sea means small, not zero.

True for the score the probe defines itself (line 212, signed): for -u_T_perp^E it gives 0.826 where the two-sided |rsi| - max |foreign| gives 0.141. But: (1) neither round uses a signed score. Round 1's D4 is |c| - max |cos_x| (rk_verdict.py:74). Round 2's OD-C6 is the absolute change of the mean projection on each foreign axis (plan lines 1624-1626; r2_unlearn_qwen.py:133-139 and 222-223). (2) The README's example fails. u_T_perp^J scores -0.06/-0.05 under the signed and the two-sided score alike, because its tone effect exceeds its RSI effect, not because the score rewards an anti-component. (3) 'Foreign effect about 0' is met by neither axis in T4 (u_T_perp^E up to 0.39, u_T_perp^J 0.78). The count is right: one exact string ('myself') is shared between the two top-15 lists (line 157). 'Almost disjoint' overstates it. By word family the lists share learn- (Learned, learnt, learned, learn, learner against learning) and myself. The statistic is exact-string overlap among the top 15 of 93,898 tokens, duplicates are not removed (the J-lens list has 14 distinct strings), and there is no baseline from other directions. J[14] is far from the identity (||J - I|| / ||I|| = 3.2 in Frobenius norm), so different top words are expected for any direction at this depth. The number therefore says nothing specific about this axis or about the feedback loop.

JSON T2: cosine 0.991 between the filtered and unfiltered u_T_perp (0.966-0.996 for the single axes), 12-16 % non-semantic tokens; the T4 rows of the filtered axis differ from the unfiltered ones by at most 0.03. Caveats: the filtered mean shares 84-88 % of its tokens with the unfiltered one, so a high cosine is close to automatic; the filter is a letter-or-digit test plus a norm cap (line 122); T3 was not repeated for the filtered axis.

True part: the controls use Euclidean cosines and projections (rk_loop.py:286 and 317; r2_unlearn_qwen.py:128-139). Not true: README lines 14-15 say the foreign cosines are zero by construction and that no indicator can see the effect. Only cos(u_T_perp, foreign axis) of the start direction is zero by construction. The cos_sports/tone/sea/u_neg rows are taken on the derived direction, the mean read-back difference of the generated + and - texts (rk_loop.py:285, 314, 317), which is not orthogonalised; round 1's D4 uses their absolute values (rk_verdict.py:74). Round 2's OD-C6 is the absolute change of the mean projection of the generated texts on each foreign text axis (plan lines 1624-1626). These are two-sided, text-level measurements in the reading frame: if a counter-push made the texts more like sports texts, they would move. What they do not measure is the lens-metric overlap of the push vector, which is a write-side quantity. The probe measured none of these controls (it generated no text under a push), so 'blind' is an inference. Whether the round-1 rows show a foreign shift is in the round-1 outputs, which I did not open. A shift of the size seen in T4 may be too small to show in 40-token texts, but that would be a matter of size, not of the metric.

issues.title: By the probe's own use test the J-metric-perpendicular axis is the less neutral one
issues.detail: Sign-following foreign effects (half the difference of the + and - rows of T4): u_T_perp^E -0.27 / -0.23 / -0.18 (largest = 0.43 x the RSI effect, rms 0.23); u_T_perp^J +0.03 / +0.06 / +0.71 (largest = 1.08 x the RSI effect, rms 0.41). Two-sided score |rsi| - max |foreign|: +0.58 / +0.14 for u_T_perp^E, -0.06 / -0.05 for u_T_perp^J. README line 42 calls u_T_perp^J the more neutral axis and blames its bad score on the score. Consequences: no support for replacing the Euclidean orthogonalisation by an M_J one, and exact M_J-orthogonality to the tone axis (cosine 5e-17) did not predict use (tone words +0.71), which counts against calling M_J 'the metric the model reads with'.

issues.title: The lens metric is dominated by few gain directions, the four foreign axes are nearly one direction in it, and the null is isotropic
issues.detail: Measured on the lens file: J[14] has singular values 102.7, 20.2, 16.9, ... with median 0.98; the first carries 45 % of the squared Frobenius norm (participation ratio of J^T J 4.9; its entropy rank is 58.7, so the probe's reported entropy rank of 227 for M_J does not exclude a dominant direction). Its output vector is the same at blocks 10-18 (|cos| >= 0.999) and sits in about 19 coordinates. With the unembedding Gram replaced by the identity, four random axes capture 0.23 (mean) and 0.57-0.58 (95th percentile) of random Euclid-perpendicular directions; 0.018 / 0.043 once that one direction is removed from the metric. This shows the mechanism, not that it explains 0.345: the real metric also contains the unembedding, which I did not load. From the JSON: the baseline 0.09 is about 45 times isotropic; the largest eigenvalue of the foreign axes' M_J correlation matrix is at least 2.61 of 4 (a one-factor model with mutual |cos| 0.7-0.8 reproduces 0.345). The comparison with 200 isotropic directions (lines 169-172) is therefore not a fair null for a text-contrast direction.

issues.title: T3 is in-sample: no cross-fitting, no bootstrap, and the axes are a new text sample
issues.detail: The same estimated axes are projected out in the Euclidean metric and then used to measure the overlap in M_J (lines 149-151, 163-168). In the Euclidean metric the estimation noise of a foreign axis cancels by construction; in an anisotropic metric it does not. Synthetic check with true lens-metric overlap 0, one gain direction and Euclidean noise-to-signal 0.2: measured M-cosine -0.05 when the axis does not load on the gain direction, +0.29 and +0.69 when it loads 0.2 and 0.6. The sign of the bias depends on whether the lens amplifies the axes' noise more than their signal, which is unknown here. Round 1 has prompt folds (rk_loop.py:214-222); the probe does not use them. If round 1 ran on GPU the texts differ from round 1's (CPU generator at probe line 70, device generator at rk_loop.py:124), so the numbers are one new draw. The README admits the missing bootstrap for T4 only (line 51).

issues.title: T4 has no control word sets, no control directions and no error bars, and part of the reported rise does not depend on the sign of the push
issues.detail: Half the sum of the + and - rows is +0.06 to +0.12 for every word set under every direction, including RSI words (u_T_perp^E: +0.106, +0.113, +0.097, +0.123; u_T_perp^J: +0.062 to +0.078; raw u_T: +0.065 to +0.100), although KL scales as alpha^2.0 in the two tries of each row, i.e. the pushes are small. The normaliser alone would contribute about -0.05 (minus the KL) to every token, so the positive value most plausibly arises because the tokens of a set respond unequally and the log of a sum is convex (my inference). The effect measure is line 200. Without random word sets matched in base probability and random directions at matched damage, a topic-specific leak cannot be told from a generic redistribution; without per-sequence errors, 0.2-0.3 cannot be told from noise.

issues.title: The tone word set contains '!', which the readout filter removes from the metric
issues.detail: Line 53 keeps only tokens with a Latin letter or digit: 93,898 of 151,936 rows. It drops all 25,557 rows with CJK characters, 32,214 other rows (all punctuation and whitespace tokens, including '!', '.', the line breaks) and 267 empty rows, and it keeps the 26 control tokens such as <|im_start|> and <think>. M_J is built from the kept rows only (lines 54-58), and line 55 centres over them, so a shift of all letter tokens against punctuation is invisible too. The tone set of T4 (line 181) starts with '!' (id 0). The finding that the M_J-perpendicular axis is not neutral for tone can therefore be a mismatch between the metric's vocabulary and the test set. All 34 words are single tokens and no id is shared between sets.

issues.title: T4 is not the round-1 or C-Q2 setting
issues.detail: T4 scores next-token probabilities on unpushed plain-prompt reference texts under teacher forcing (lines 190-201). Round 1 generates under the push and reads the texts back; C-Q2 generates instructed pro and anti texts under -alpha_u and reads them on fixed axes (plan 1199-1219). The statement that counter-steering in Part C pushes the model toward the control topics (README lines 37-38) is an extrapolation from a first-order next-token readout to generated, instructed text.

issues.title: Calling M_J 'the metric the model reads with' is an idealisation
issues.detail: The Gram counts each kept token equally; what the output distribution responds to is the probability-weighted covariance diag(p) - p p^T, which differs by position. The lens is an average Jacobian fitted on raw wikitext in 128-token windows (config.yaml), stored in fp16, and it sums the effect of a one-position perturbation over the current and all later target positions (library README lines 16-22), while T4 reads each position under a push at all positions. The repo's own earlier sanity log shows how rough the lens is at this depth: at blocks 12 and 18 it matches the model's next token in 0 of 6 prompts, median rank 122 and 79 (/home/user/DSSE/results/ju_space/extract.log, lines 2-3). One worry I could test came out small: the final norm's radial projector, which the linear form ignores, removes 1.6 % of the squared size of the lens's top mode and 0.6 % for random directions at 205 saved pre-norm final states (last prompt token).

issues.title: Top-15 overlap is a brittle statistic
issues.detail: Line 157 intersects sets of stripped token strings from top_words (lines 60-61), which does not merge case or word forms. Shared word families: learn- and myself. No baseline from other axes or random directions, although J[14] differs from the identity by 3.2 in relative Frobenius norm.

issues.title: Damage calibration differs from round 1 and round 2
issues.detail: Probe: mean KL over all 64 references (lines 190, 199), each direction and each sign matched separately (202-213). Round 1: first 8 references, all RSI-topic prompts (rk_loop.py:186-190), one alpha calibrated on +unit(u_T) and used for every direction and both signs (240-246, 312). Round 2 C-Q2: one alpha per direction from the + sign (plan 1201-1203). The probe's alphas span 0.0865-0.100, so sizes shift by at most about 15 %; no sign change. The cap uses the median norm over continuation tokens (line 115) instead of user-content plus continuation tokens (rk_loop.py:173-174); it only acts on outlier positions.

issues.title: matched() returns an untested alpha when no try lands in the band
issues.detail: Lines 202-208: after the sixth miss the loop still updates alpha, and the function returns that new alpha together with the damage and effect of the previous one, without an in-band flag. rk_loop.set_alpha keeps the closest try and stores in_band (lines 245-246). Not triggered in this run: all eight rows are inside 0.045-0.055 after one or two tries, and alpha and damage equal the last tried pair.

issues.title: Reproducibility gaps
issues.detail: The defaults (NP 12, NNEW 32, line 25) are not the reported run; the README's command (line 69) sets NP and NNEW only in a comment. The axes cache is keyed by the output path alone (lines 126-128), so a short test followed by a full run with the same output path would silently reuse the short-test axes; the delivered JSON is not affected (its token counts are integers over 64 x 2 x 40). Library versions are not recorded, although the meaning of a GenerationConfig with do_sample=False passed next to a model config with do_sample=True, temperature 0.6, top_k 20 has changed between transformers versions (under the 5.22.2 installed here it stays greedy, which Gumbel-max needs). The JSON stores no per-token effects, no foreign Gram, no top eigenvalue shares, and the axes were not delivered.

issues.title: The lens file carries no provenance field
issues.detail: README_hf.md describes a 'provenance' entry with the capture point; the file has only J, n_prompts, source_layers (0..26) and d_model. It holds 27 maps, not 28. The pairing of J[b] with the output of block b rests on the README wording, the map count, this repo's earlier scripts and the U-Space reference code, which all agree. An off-by-one would matter: J[13] and J[15] differ from J[14] by 53-54 % in Frobenius norm.

recommendations: Treat the probe as a hypothesis, not as a finding to build on. Do not adopt M_J-perpendicular axes: in T4 they move tone words as much as RSI words.

To test C1 and C2 with the model (same script, CPU): store the 4x4 M_J Gram of the foreign axes; eigen-decompose M_J and report, for u_T_perp and each foreign axis, the share of its M_J norm on the top 1, 5 and 20 eigen-directions; recompute shares and cosines with the top direction(s) removed; decode the top and bottom words of the foreign component F (c_E - c_M) and of each foreign axis; repeat with J[13] and J[15] and with a probability-weighted Gram at the T4 positions.

Replace the isotropic baseline by text-contrast nulls: the sign-flip null axes of the RSI differences projected like u_T_perp (rk_loop.py:223 and 226), and each foreign axis made Euclid-perpendicular to the others. Cross-fit over round 1's prompt folds (axes from one fold, overlap measured against axes from the other) and bootstrap prompts for an interval on 0.345 and on the cosines.

To test C3 and C4: add at least 20 random word sets matched in base log-probability and the null directions of rk_dirs at matched damage; report the sign-following and the sign-independent part separately, per token; take '!' out of the tone set or put punctuation into the metric; bootstrap over the 64 sequences and split RSI-topic from scene prompts; add a short generation test under + and - push with read-back on the foreign text axes, which is the quantity OD-C6 uses.

Someone with access to the round-1 outputs should look at the sign and size of cos_sports, cos_tone and cos_sea of d_1 in the RSI loops (rk_loop.py:317). A text-level shift toward the foreign topics under the counter-push would show there as negative cosines; round 2's C-Q2 (c) separates the counter side.
Keep the existing two-sided rules (rk_verdict.py:74; OD-C6). If a stricter demand than 'less than half the concept' is wanted, state a tolerance in gap units; neither axis meets 'about 0' in T4.

If M_J is reported in round 2 as a descriptive extra, restrict it to push vectors and report it with the mode decomposition. Applying it to read-back quantities such as OD-C6 or the cos_* rows would mix the write and read roles the README itself wants kept apart.

Before any re-run of the probe: make matched() keep the closest try and store an in-band flag; key the cache by NP, NNEW and BLOCK; put NP=32 NNEW=40 into the command; record library versions; save the axes.
reports.summary:
Bottom line (construction lens). mlpp_probe.py computes what its formulas say, and its axes are a faithful re-implementation of round 1's recipe. I found no code error that changes a number in mlpp_probe_b14.json. What does not hold is part of the reading: (a) the README's statement that the foreign cosines are zero by construction and that no existing indicator can see the effect (C8) is wrong for round 1's loop rows and for round 2's OD-C6; (b) by the probe's own use test the J-metric-perpendicular axis is the less neutral one (tone words move 1.08 times as much as RSI words), so it is no better control axis and the README's argument for C5 fails; (c) the lens-metric result (C1, C2) and the use test (C3, C4) lack the controls needed to call them a leak toward the control topics. Nothing was re-run with the model; the J-lens numbers themselves could not be recomputed (they need the unembedding and the axes, and no axes cache was delivered). The README is candid about several limits (lines 51-53).

1. Faithfulness to round 1. Same as rk_loop.py: all 64 prompts in the same order (probe line 35 with NP=32 = rk_loop.py:77; the JSON's non-semantic token counts are integers over 64 x 2 x 40, so the axes come from the full run); instructions (134 vs 204); keys keyseed('axis', name, p) shared by pro and anti, keyseed('ref', p) (134, 114 vs 204, 165); Gumbel-max at T 0.7 (69-72 vs 123-126); 40 new tokens; reading under the plain prompt at the output of block 14, mean over continuation tokens, empty texts dropped (96-108, 118-124, 137-138 vs 145-156, 217-218); NEG axis as negated minus plain replies to 'Say one sentence.' (142-144 vs 158-160, 211). The projection is the same: rk_loop's QR projector (224-226) and the probe's normal-equation projector (63-65, 150) are both the joint projection on the span, not an ordered Gram-Schmidt (difference 7e-16 on synthetic data). The push formula and positions equal rk_loop.damage (184-188 vs 102-110, 194). Differences:
- New text sample if round 1 ran on GPU (CPU generator, line 70, vs device generator, rk_loop.py:124). Sizes can move; a sign change of the large effects is unlikely but untested (no bootstrap).
- Cap from the median norm over continuation tokens (115) instead of user-content plus continuation tokens (rk_loop.py:173-174). Negligible.
- Damage averaged over all 64 references (190, 199) instead of the first 8, all RSI-topic prompts (rk_loop.py:186-190). Changes alpha only.
- Each direction and each sign matched separately (202-213); round 1 uses one alpha from +unit(u_T) for everything (rk_loop.py:240-246, 312), round 2 C-Q2 one per direction from the + sign. Alphas here span 0.0865-0.100: at most about 15 % in size, no sign change.
- T4 is teacher-forced on unpushed plain-prompt texts; round 1 and C-Q2 generate under the push and read back. A different quantity.
- Defaults (NP 12, NNEW 32, line 25) differ from the reported run; batch size and float precision are immaterial.

2. Lenses. J[14] is the right map for the output of block 14. README_hf.md ('every block before the target layer', target = final block), the file (27 maps, keys 0..26, for 28 blocks; ||J[26] - I|| / ||I|| = 0.5248 = config.yaml's final_identity_distance), this repo's scripts (extract.py:21, 29-30; axes.py:14; analyze2.py:13; mim_common.py:25-26; neu_static.py:79-81) and the U-Space reference code (pipeline_04_forward.py:35, 51-52 with src_uspace.py:61, 76) all pair J[b] with the forward-hook output of block b. The file has no provenance field, so this rests on those sources. M_J = J^T GU J is what the text says (lines 54-58). 'W_U diag(g) J' is the form the repo and the reference use to decode directions. It ignores the final norm's 1/rms scale and radial projector (measured: the projector removes 1.6 % of the squared size of the lens's top mode at 205 saved final states, so this is small), probability weighting (each of 93,898 kept tokens counts equally), the fact that the lens sums a one-position perturbation's effect over the current and all later positions, the fit corpus (raw wikitext) and nonlinearity. Centring is the right kind of operation, but it is done over the kept rows only, so a shift of all letter tokens against punctuation and CJK tokens is invisible. Two measured facts matter for T3: J[14] has one direction with 45 % of its squared norm (sigma 102.7, median 0.98), and in a J-only metric that direction alone gives unrelated random directions a 'foreign share' of 0.23 on average against four random axes.

3. Code. perpM, cosM, the M-orthogonal projector and the share formula are correct. The baseline is 200 isotropic directions, the same draws for every metric (169-172). top_words does not de-duplicate. All 34 words are single tokens and no id is shared between sets, but '!' in the tone set is outside the vocabulary on which M_J is defined (line 53). The steer hook is registered once (189), after all generation and reading; the capture hook is inert in T4; the base pass is unpushed (185); the push is reset after every call (201). matched() returns a never-tested alpha when no try lands in the band (202-208); not triggered here. The effect is the change of the log of a word set's summed probability, averaged over positions, then sequences (200-201).

Needs the model: C1, C2 (recompute, mode decomposition, cross-fitted or bootstrapped axes, text-contrast nulls), C3, C4 (control word sets and directions, per-token effects, generation), C6 (longer lists, other directions). C8 needs the round-1 loop outputs, which I did not open. C5 and C7 need nothing further.

final.summary:
The probe's main conclusion is not established. It has three parts.

1. **"The Euclidean orthogonalisation over-subtracts."** In the J-lens metric this is true by construction: it is measured relative to the probe's own M_J projection. In the use test there is one run in which u_T_perp^E moves all three foreign word sets against its RSI effect, by 28-43 % of that effect. There is no null, no neutral word set, no interval and no generated text.
2. **"Counter-steering actively pushes the model toward the control topics."** Not shown. 29-41 % of the headline numbers is a rise that a push of either sign produces in every word set, RSI words included. The remaining 0.18-0.27 nats is a first-order next-token shift on teacher-forced text, and the axis comparison the README uses to rule out redistribution only shows something expected (u_J differs from u_E exactly by foreign-axis content).
3. **"The foreign-axis controls cannot see it."** Wrong. The deciding controls of both rounds are two-sided and read generated texts or exact gradients (K8, K5, OD-C6).

What survives is a testable hypothesis. Round 2's C-Q2 already tests its text-level form at the same 0.05-nat damage, and its part (c) stores the direct text analogue of the probe's sign-following effects.

**The reviewers' numbers hold.** I recomputed every figure from the JSON that I relied on, and all match:
- odd and even parts, the specificity scores, and the zero crossings at 89 / 80 / 20 %
- the 38 % foreign-span part of raw u_T's RSI response
- lambda_max >= 2.61 and mean sign-aligned M_J cosine >= 0.52
- top-15 overlaps of 1 / 3 / 4 / 3 / 3 / 6
- the three double-rounded README figures

With the tokenizer only, I confirmed that '!' (id 0) is the only one of the 34 word-set tokens outside the metric's vocabulary, and that all 34 are single tokens. From the lens file I confirmed 27 maps, no provenance key, sigma 102.68 / 20.19, top share 0.449, and the 53 % differences of J[13] and J[15] from J[14].

**Where the reviewers disagree or go too far, and how I decided:**
- **C4:** I side with reviewers 1 and 2 ("partly") over reviewer 3 ("supported"), because of '!'.
- **Which perpendicular axis is more neutral:** all three say u_E; reviewer 1 rates it as changing a conclusion. That rests entirely on the tone set. On sports and sea the J-perpendicular axis is closer to zero, and without tone its score beats u_E's (+0.60 vs +0.36). Neither axis is shown to be more neutral. What stands is that T4 gives no support for M_J-based orthogonalisation.
- **What the J-lens reads:** reviewer 1 is right that the fit sums over current and future positions. Reviewer 2's "both read the same position" is wrong, but its conclusion about README point 4 stands.
- **C-Q2's push calibration:** reviewer 3 is right that the code calibrates on the counter-push (r2_unlearn_qwen.py:869-873). Reviewer 1's "from the + sign" is wrong.
- **Strength of the lens anisotropy:** J[14]'s dominant mode sits on three output coordinates (1793, 1999, 1683). Without them the entropy rank is 265, close to the 227 the probe reports for M_J. So reviewer 1's J-only figures overstate it, and reviewer 2's scale of 10-17 % of the trace is the better reading. Nobody has checked how the readout weights those coordinates.
- **Round-1 cos_* rows as a test:** reviewer 2 predicts clearly negative values, but the RSI content's own overlap with the foreign axes can mask the effect. A negative value would support the probe; a zero one would not refute it. K5's z on u_T_perp for sports is the cleaner existing test.
- **Line numbers:** r2_unlearn_qwen.py changed during the review. Reviewer 3's line numbers match the current file; reviewers 1 and 2 cite an older version with the same content.

Nothing in the repository was changed. No model weights were loaded, no round-1 output was read, and no web access was used.
